title: Question 5
stem:
An electron is travelling in a straight line through a vacuum with a constant speed of 1.5 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.
The electron enters a uniform electric field at point A, as shown in Fig. 5.1.
The electron continues to move in the same direction until it is brought to rest by the electric field at point B. Distance AB is 2.0 cm.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the direction of the electric field.

markscheme_points.text: to the right / from the left / from A to B / in the same direction as electron velocity

hints: Hint 1: Consider the physical mechanism underlying this process based on electric field strength and acceleration.
parts.proper_answer: to the right / from the left / from A to B / in the same direction as electron velocity
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
Identify the core physical principle governing this problem: Electric field strength and acceleration. State the relevant formula or theoretical relationship clearly.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Substitute the known quantities into the formula with correct SI units and powers of ten:
$$to the right / from the left / from A to B / in the same direction as electron velocity$$
Work through the intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
